description: Only films whose replacement cost is 20.99 or higher are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are included.

b.request: For each rating, among films with `replacement_cost >= 20.99`, calculate the average `rental_duration` and the average of each film’s `rental_rate / replacement_cost`, ignoring missing values; then return one unrounded row containing the average of the per-rating duration averages followed by the average of the per-rating ratio averages.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_duration) AS avg_rating_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_rating_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating
b.raw: For each rating, among films with `replacement_cost >= 20.99`, calculate the average `rental_duration` and the average of each film’s `rental_rate / replacement_cost`, ignoring missing values; then return one unrounded row containing the average of the per-rating duration averages followed by the average of the per-rating ratio averages.

a.request: Considering only films whose `replacement_cost` is at least 20.99, work out for each `rating` the average `rental_duration` and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` (ignoring missing values). Then return a single row with the average of those per-rating average durations and the average of those per-rating average ratios, in that order and unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_duration) AS avg_rating_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_rating_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating;

d.request: For films with `replacement_cost >= 20.99`, calculate each `rating`’s average `rental_duration` and average of `rental_rate / replacement_cost`, ignoring missing values; return one row containing the unrounded average of the per-rating duration averages followed by the unrounded average of the per-rating ratio averages.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_duration) AS avg_rating_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_rating_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating

c.request: For the pricier-to-replace films, with 20.99 as the `replacement_cost` cutoff, what are the average `rental_duration` and the average `rental_rate`-to-`replacement_cost` ratio for each `rating` (ignoring missing values)? Then give me one row with the average of those per-rating durations and the average of those per-rating ratios, in that order and unrounded. Only films whose replacement cost is 20.99 or higher are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are included.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(rental_rate / NULLIF(replacement_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 AND rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating;
